summary: This sermon examines Christian patience as two-fold: extending grace to difficult people and enduring difficult circumstances. In a culture of instant gratification and cancel culture, the preacher argues that true patience flows from understanding how patient God has been with us through our rebellion and sin. Jesus perfectly modeled this patience through His crucifixion, forgiving even those who killed Him.
key_points: Patience means not grumbling but extending grace to difficult people
Patience means enduring suffering like Job and the prophets
We underestimate God's patience toward us and withhold it from others
God's character is slow to anger and abounding in steadfast love
Jesus perfectly demonstrated patience at the cross, forgiving His accusers
big_idea: Christian patience—extending grace to difficult people and enduring difficult circumstances—is produced by the Holy Spirit as we grasp how patient God has been with us and trust His promised restoration.
title: Exercising Patience
